description: A Euclidean sequencer: it spreads a chosen number of filled steps as evenly as it can over a chosen length, and walks through them on a clock

params.text: Rotates the pattern around its length, moving where the filled steps fall without changing how many there are
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before it comes round again, 1 to 32
Sets what the output does: repeat the voltage at the clock input on a filled step, put out nothing, or flip a 10V gate over every time the pattern changes between filled and empty
Sets how many of the steps are filled, from one of them to all of them, spread as evenly over the length as the two numbers allow
Sets how much of the length CV reaches the length, none at the far left and its full 31 steps at the far right
Sets how much of the fill CV reaches the fill, none at the far left and the whole of the fill knob's travel at the far right

inputs.text: A rising edge past 2V sends the sequence back to the step the rotation knob picks
Shifts the length, 10V covering all 31 steps at full attenuation, added to the length knob and held between 1 and 32
Adds to the fill knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel at full attenuation, and the total is held between one filled step and all of them
Advances the sequence on each rising edge past 2V

outputs.text: Carries the sequence, shaped by the mode switch

notes: nothing moves until a clock is patched; the module has no clock of its own
in the repeating setting the output copies the voltage present at the clock input rather than putting out a fixed 10V, so a 5V clock gives a 5V sequence
on the hardware the mode switch doubles as a reset; in this version it does not

inputs.0:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.2:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.3:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
